claims.claim: The ancients held that the labor of the body necessitated by its needs is slavish, and they justified slavery precisely on the grounds that occupations serving life's maintenance are slavish in nature.
claims.supporting_excerpt: all ancient estimates of human activities, including those which, like Hesiod, supposedly praise labor, rest on the conviction that the labor of our body which is necessitated by its needs is slavish. Hence, occupations which did not consist in laboring, yet were undertaken not for their own sake but in order to provide the necessities of life, were assimilated to the status of labor... It was precisely on these grounds that the institution of slavery was defended and justified.

claims.claim: The modern age glorified labor as the source of all values and elevated the animal laborans to the position traditionally held by the animal rationale, yet failed to clearly distinguish between animal laborans and homo faber.
claims.supporting_excerpt: the modern age—with its reversal of all traditions... with its glorification of labor as the source of all values and its elevation of the animal laborans to the position traditionally held by the animal rationale —should not have brought forth a single theory in which animal laborans and homo faber , “the labour of our body and the work of our hands,” are clearly distinguished.

definitions.definition: One, at best the highest, of the animal species which populate the earth, characterized by being totally subject to biological necessity and labor.

distinctions.distinction: The distinction between the private household (where the slave and household inmate resided) and the public political realm (of the citizen and household head) overshadowed and predetermined all other distinctions in classical antiquity.

must_not_be_lost: Slavery in antiquity was not originally a device for cheap labor or profit, but an attempt to exclude labor from the conditions of man's life.
output.segment_function: To analyze the historical and philosophical status of labor, slavery, and the distinction between the private and public realms in antiquity and their transformation in the modern age.
